items.title: 2027: ‘Ignore opposition tactics’, APC chieftain urges Tinubu to focus on governance
items.description: A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Osun, Olatunbosun Oyintiloye, has urged President Bola Tinubu not to be distracted by opposition tactics ahead of the 2027 general elections. Oyintiloye said the President should instead focus on governance and tackle security threats identified by security agencies head-on. The APC chieftain made the call while speaking with newsmen on Sunday in Osogbo, against the backdrop of recent security alerts over possible attacks on vulnerable locations, particularly in parts of southern Nigeria. Oyintiloye said the President should urgently support security agencies to intensify surveillance, strengthen inter-agency collaboration and take proactive measures to safeguard lives and property amid emerging security concerns. He said security agencies should be reinforced through heightened vigilance, improved intelligence gathering and coordinated preventive action nationwide. Oyintiloye, a former lawmaker, also called on relevant security agencies to work closely together, share intelligence and strengthen surveillance and rapid-response mechanisms. He particularly urged increased security around schools, places of worship, National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) facilities, parks, garages and other vulnerable locations, especially with schools in session. The APC chieftain also called for an immediate, thorough and transparent investigation into the recent killings in Osun. He urged security agencies to identify all persons suspected to have participated in, sponsored or facilitated the violence. Oyintiloye said anyone against whom sufficient evidence was established should be prosecuted in accordance with the law. He appealed to all stakeholders, including transport workers, community leaders, traditional rulers and religious leaders, to remain calm and cooperate with security agencies by providing credible information that could assist investigations and prevent further violence. Oyintiloye also called for stronger security intelligence through adequate training, equipment and resources to enable security agencies to forestall, prevent, detect and respond effectively to attacks by armed groups. “If necessary, service chiefs should review and adjust their operational strategies without hesitation, as time is of the essence,” he added. He also called on state governors to complement the President’s efforts by providing adequate support and resources to security agencies within their jurisdictions. While acknowledging the President’s constitutional role as Chief Security Officer of the nation, Oyintiloye emphasised that governors and local government chairmen were closer to the grassroots and must take proactive measures to strengthen local intelligence and maintain peace. He stressed that no nation could achieve meaningful development in an atmosphere of insecurity, noting that economic growth, infrastructure development, investment and social services thrive only in a peaceful environment. “A nation with a strong and effective security system is better positioned for accelerated development, economic prosperity and sustainable social services,” he said. He urged citizens to remain vigilant, cooperate with security agencies by providing timely and useful information, and continue to pray for peace, unity and progress in the country. Oyintiloye expressed confidence in the professionalism, competence and dedication of Nigeria’s security personnel, noting that they possessed the capacity to flush out criminal elements and restore lasting peace. items.title: Tunisie | Les ventes automobiles en hausse de 14% à fin août 2026
items.description: Le marché automobile en Tunisie a connu une reprise notable au cours des huit premiers mois de 2026. Le volume total des ventes et acquisitions de véhicules (marchés officiel et parallèle) a augmenté de 13,78 %, atteignant 69 982 unités, contre 61 505 unités sur la même période en 2025. Selon les statistiques de la Chambre nationale des concessionnaires et constructeurs automobiles — relevant de l’Union tunisienne de l’industrie, du commerce et de l’artisanat (Utica) — arrêtées à fin août 2026, les concessionnaires agréés sur le marché tunisien ont écoulé 47 002 véhicules, soit 67 % de la part totale du marché. Cela représente une hausse de 11,69 % par rapport aux 42 082 véhicules vendus durant la même période de l’année précédente. Les ventes de voitures via les circuits parallèles — incluant les ré-immatriculations et l’utilisation de l’avantage fiscal accordé aux Tunisiens résidant à l’étranger (FCR) — ont enregistré une hausse notable de 18,31 %, portant le total des véhicules immatriculés par ce biais à 22 980 unités (contre 19 423 jusqu’en août 2025), soit l’équivalent de 33 % du volume total du marché automobile en Tunisie (contre 32 % l’année précédente). L’article Tunisie | Les ventes automobiles en hausse de 14% à fin août 2026 est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: N3.4bn drug bust: NDLEA arrests fake police, mechanic
items.description: Records major drug seizures across eight states, FCT By Olasunkanmi Akoni ABUJA — Operatives of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency, NDLEA, have intercepted more than 1.3 million pills and capsules of tramadol and other opioids, as well as 6,000kg of cannabis, in a series of operations across eight states and the Federal Capital Territory. The agency said the seizures had a combined street value of more than N3.4 billion. The operations were conducted in Lagos, Edo, Niger, Delta, Ondo, Gombe and Imo states, as well as the FCT. The NDLEA Chairman, Brig. Gen. Mohamed Buba Marwa (retd.), commended officers of the various commands for what he described as professionalism and intelligence-driven operations, urging them to sustain the agency’s balanced approach to drug control. A major highlight of the operations was the interception of 1,200 parcels of Canadian Loud, a potent strain of cannabis, weighing 603.75kg and valued at N1.811 billion. The operation also led to the arrest of a 49-year-old suspected drug trafficker, Innocent Ekpe, who allegedly impersonated a senior police officer to evade scrutiny at checkpoints while transporting illicit drugs across state lines. Ekpe was arrested on Wednesday, September 16, along the Benin-Onitsha Expressway in Asaba, Delta State, with 292.48kg of skunk concealed in his silver Toyota Sienna bus. According to the agency, preliminary investigation revealed that Ekpe allegedly presented himself as Godwin Emeka, a Deputy Superintendent of Police, using a forged police identification card. A 39-year-old alleged accomplice, Nduka Joseph, was also arrested. In Edo State, NDLEA operatives acting on intelligence raided a location along Agbor Road, Benin City, where they arrested 45-year-old Matthew Ossai. The agency said Ossai allegedly used his auto-repair workshop to store illicit drugs. Operatives recovered 48kg of Canadian Loud, 152 grammes of methamphetamine and a metal box allegedly used to store the substances. At the Tin-Can Island Port in Lagos, NDLEA operatives placed a 40-foot container shipped from Montreal, Canada, under surveillance after it arrived on September 12. A joint physical examination conducted with the Nigeria Customs Service and other security agencies on Wednesday, September 16, led to the discovery of 1,200 parcels of Canadian Loud weighing 603.75kg. The consignment was concealed inside 31 black jumbo bags loaded into two Toyota Sienna vehicles in the container. In Niger State, three suspects — Bashir Usman, 20; Abubakar Nuhu, 18; and Abdulrahman Abdulwahab, 18 — were arrested on Tuesday, September 15, during a patrol along the Abuja-Kaduna Expressway at Chachi, Tafa Local Government Area. The suspects were allegedly found with two locally fabricated AK-47 rifles and a magazine, a locally made pistol with a magazine, and nine rounds of 9mm ammunition concealed in a black travel bag. Two other suspects, Aminu Isyaku, 23, and Jamilu Habibu, 25, were arrested on Friday, September 18, along the Abaji-Abuja Highway. The agency said more than 1.1 million assorted tramadol tablets and capsules, codeine syrup, methamphetamine and Exol tablets were recovered from them. The substances were allegedly concealed in eight sacks and were being transported from Onitsha, Anambra State, to Mararaba, Nasarawa State. In Lagos, NDLEA operatives arrested Onyeka Ofor at his residence in Aguda, Surulere, on Friday, September 18, with 48,900 pills of tramadol 225mg. Seven cartons of cannabis sativa weighing 59kg were also intercepted at a logistics company in the state, leading to the arrest of a suspect identified as Luke Ugokwe. In another operation in Lagos, 43-year-old Ibrahim Hudu was arrested at Apongbo on Thursday, September 17, with 998.38kg of nitrous oxide gas. In Gombe State, a total of 154,480 capsules of tramadol were recovered from two suspects, Sabi’u Umar, 27, and Hassana Muhammad, 19. The suspects were arrested at the Barunde area and Gombe Main Market respectively on Friday, September 18. In Imo State, 25-year-old Ifesinachi Godwin was arrested along the Owerri-Onitsha Road on Friday with 43.85kg of skunk. Similarly, four suspects — Blessing Effiong, Saviour Peter, David Friday Sunday and Ability Peter Sunday — were arrested during a raid on a two-hectare cannabis farm in Ita-Ogbolu Forest, Ondo State, on Tuesday, September 15. The NDLEA said 5,000kg of skunk was destroyed during the operation, while 48kg of dried and fresh cannabis was recovered from the location. Meanwhile, commands and formations of the agency continued their War Against Drug Abuse, WADA, sensitisation campaigns across the country during the week. The activities included enlightenment lectures for students and staff of St. Ferdinand School, Ogbomoso, Oyo State; Unizik Secondary School, Awka, Anambra State; Scholars Nursery and Primary School, Epe, Lagos State; and Government Technical Training School, Jalingo, Taraba State. The Delta Ports Command also paid a WADA advocacy visit to traditional ruler, King Couple Mackson Oromoni Mobene III, Pere Ama-Okosu of Ogbe-Ijoh Warri Kingdom, Delta State. The NDLEA said the sensitisation activities were part of its continued efforts to raise awareness about the dangers of illicit drug use and trafficking. items.title: Akpabio in Italy prays for banditry, terrorism to end in Nigeria
items.description: By Henry Umoru Ahead of the 2027 presidential and general elections, the President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio, visited the Prayer Ground of St. Padre Pio at St Giovanni Rotondo in Italy to pray for peaceful 2027 elections and an end to banditry and terrorism in Nigeria. Answering questions from St. Padre PIO TV/ Radio in Italy, Akpabio said, “We are all from Nigeria. We came to offer prayers and get blessings from God for ourselves, families and our dear country that is currently being ravaged by banditry and terrorism. “We are here on this prayer ground, and we are going home fulfilled, that we were able to touch this Holy ground, drop our intentions, which he will take to God on our behalf”. In a statement by his Special Assistant on Media, Jackson Udom, Akpabio described the ground as a holy one, noting that ” I am very impressed that the place has been well kept. This is a Holy ground. Some people who are here might not even understand the significance of this ground but those of us who are adherents and followers of PIO, believe in his intercessions.” To further buttress his belief in the efficacy of the name; PIO, Akpabio disclosed how St PIO interceded for the miraculous healing of his wife, Mrs. Unoma Akpabio, after she was 98 percent dead. According to him, “My wife was in a coma for six months in a hospital in Germany. She was 98 percent dead. I used the picture of PIO to make a sign of the cross on her, instead of putting off the life- support machine she was on. She had an operation that went wrong. I cried to Mother Mary, the mother of Jesus Christ and called on PIO to intercede. “Miraculously, she woke up. That hospital, up to today, is yet to understand what happened. As someone who has experienced the power of where I am standing, I understand it more than anyone else. ” This is my 10th time here. When my wife was finally discharged from the hospital, she waited for three months before she could remember my name and those of the children. We are here today to thank God and PIO for always interceding for us. “We honored PIO by giving our son the baptismal name; PIO. We also established a big academy, which we called PIO Football Academy, where we train and offer scholarships to children of the poor from age 9 up to university level, all in memory of PIO. May his soul rest in perfect peace.” The post Akpabio in Italy prays for banditry, terrorism to end in Nigeria appeared first on Vanguard News .

Tunisie : 126 combattants terroristes identifiés grâce à l’IA lors d’une opération d’Interpol
items.description: Une operation internationale de lutte contre le terrorisme dans l'espace numerique a permis d'identifier 126 combattants terroristes etrangers grâce notamment a des outils d'intelligence artificielle, a annonce Interpol le 18 septembre. Baptisee « Shams II », l'operation, coordonnee par Interpol du 1er au 5 juin a Tunis, a reuni 28 agents et experts specialises de 11 pays. Les enqueteurs ont extrait 108 076 images de visages a partir de contenus visuels publies par des groupes djihadistes. Des agents d'IA et des scripts automatises ont ete utilises pour accelerer la collecte et l'analyse des donnees, notamment pour eliminer les doublons et verifier la qualite des images. Le processus a permis de retenir 6 362 images faciales uniques et de bonne qualite, ensuite analysees par le systeme de reconnaissance faciale d'Interpol. Les resultats generes par l'IA ont ete soumis a une verification par des agents et analystes specialises, conformement aux regles d'Interpol relatives au traitement des donnees. Des renseignements supplementaires fournis par le Bureau central national d'Interpol a Bagdad, en Irak, ont egalement permis d'ajouter plusieurs centaines d'images a l'operation. Cryptomonnaies et jeux en ligne a ce jour, 126 combattants terroristes etrangers ont ete identifies parmi les images analysees. Ces correspondances doivent permettre d'enrichir les renseignements disponibles sur les suspects, notamment concernant leurs eventuelles localisations et leurs reseaux. Les donnees sont integrees aux bases d'Interpol. Les pistes recueillies sont deja exploitees dans le cadre de procedures judiciaires dans plusieurs pays participants, dont une affaire concernant deux combattants terroristes etrangers presumes actuellement detenus. Des milliers d'images doivent encore etre analysees. L'operation a egalement eu recours a des outils specialises dans les cryptomonnaies pour retracer des financements illicites. Trois demandes urgentes ont ainsi ete adressees a un prestataire de services sur actifs virtuels afin d'obtenir des donnees concernant des clients et de contribuer a perturber des flux de financement du terrorisme. Par ailleurs, les participants ont echange avec des representants de l'industrie du jeu video sur la radicalisation des jeunes dans les environnements en ligne. L'operation a reuni la Cote d'Ivoire, le Ghana, l'Irak, le Kenya, la Malaisie, le Nigeria, les Philippines, le Qatar, le Tadjikistan, la Tunisie et l'Ouzbekistan.

items.title: Interpol recourt à l’IA pour identifier des terroristes
items.description: Plus de 108 000 images de visages extraites de contenus diffusés en ligne par des groupes djihadistes, plus de 6 300 images sélectionnées pour analyse et 126 combattants terroristes étrangers (CTE) présumés — affiliés à des organisations terroristes — identifiés : tels sont les principaux résultats de l’opération antiterroriste Shams II, coordonnée par Interpol et menée à Tunis du 1 er au 5 juin 2026, avec la participation de 28 agents et experts issus de 11 pays. L’opération, dont les résultats ont été dévoilés cette semaine par Interpol, constitue l’un des exemples les plus récents de l’utilisation de l’intelligence artificielle (IA) pour analyser de vastes quantités de données numériques à des fins d’enquête. Au cours de ces cinq jours d’activité, les opérateurs ont extrait précisément 108 076 images de visages à partir de contenus visuels publiés par des organisations djihadistes. Des agents d’IA programmés et des scripts développés grâce à l’IA ont automatisé une partie de la collecte des données, permettant ainsi d’éliminer les doublons et de vérifier la qualité des images. Le corpus a ainsi été réduit à 6 362 images de visages uniques, suffisamment nettes pour être soumises au système de reconnaissance faciale d’Interpol. Le recours aux outils technologiques n’a toutefois pas remplacé l’analyse des enquêteurs. Interpol précise que les résultats générés par l’IA ont été vérifiés par des agents et des analystes spécialisés, dans le respect de ses règles relatives au traitement des données. Les correspondances obtenues ont ensuite servi d’éléments de renseignement et ont été recoupées avec les informations déjà disponibles sur les suspects, notamment celles concernant leurs localisations potentielles et leurs réseaux de contacts. Une contribution supplémentaire est venue du Bureau central national d’Interpol à Bagdad, qui a fourni une vaste base d’informations sur des suspects liés au terrorisme, ajoutant des centaines d’images aux éléments soumis à l’extraction et à l’analyse. Selon l’organisation internationale, des milliers d’autres images restent à examiner et pourraient ainsi ouvrir de nouvelles pistes d’enquête. Les résultats de l’opération ont déjà eu des retombées judiciaires. Interpol indique que certaines des pistes apparues au cours de ces activités sont exploitées dans le cadre de procédures judiciaires dans les pays participants, notamment dans une affaire concernant deux combattants terroristes étrangers présumés actuellement en détention. Dans son communiqué, l’organisation ne divulgue ni la nationalité des 126 personnes identifiées ni les pays où elles se trouvent ou auxquels elles sont directement liées. Par conséquent, leur identification ne permet pas d’établir un lien spécifique avec la Tunisie. Les enquêteurs ont également utilisé des outils de traçage des cryptomonnaies afin d’identifier des flux financiers liés au financement du terrorisme. Ces opérations ont conduit à l’envoi de trois demandes urgentes à un prestataire de services d’actifs virtuels (VASP) pour obtenir des données clients. Parallèlement, les représentants des 11 pays concernés ont rencontré des acteurs du secteur des jeux en ligne pour discuter des risques de radicalisation des jeunes dans les environnements numériques et des moyens de renforcer l’échange d’informations entre les autorités publiques et le secteur privé. La dimension numérique devient ainsi un axe transversal de la lutte antiterroriste, allant de la collecte d’images à la reconstitution des réseaux, jusqu’à la surveillance des canaux de financement potentiels. La Côte d’Ivoire, le Ghana, l’Irak, le Kenya, la Malaisie, le Nigéria, les Philippines, le Qatar, le Tadjikistan, la Tunisie et l’Ouzbékistan ont pris part à l’opération Shams II. La participation de pays africains, asiatiques et du Moyen-Orient reflète la dimension transnationale de l’activité d’enquête, tandis que le choix de Tunis comme base opérationnelle a permis de réunir, dans la capitale tunisienne, des spécialistes issus de divers services nationaux de lutte contre le terrorisme. Cette opération s’inscrit dans le cadre du projet CT Tech+, financé par l’Union européenne via ses instruments de politique étrangère et soutenu par le Bureau de lutte contre le terrorisme des Nations unies (Unoct). Pour Interpol, Shams II démontre qu’il est possible d’allier coopération internationale et outils d’analyse assistés par l’intelligence artificielle pour traiter des volumes de données difficilement gérables par un simple travail manuel. Le résultat le plus marquant de l’opération tunisienne est donc également d’ordre méthodologique : l’IA est utilisée pour accélérer la collecte, la sélection et le recoupement des données, alors que l’identification dans le cadre de l’enquête demeure soumise au contrôle des opérateurs. Un modèle appelé, selon Interpol, à être davantage utilisé dans les activités internationales de lutte contre les réseaux terroristes et criminels transnationaux. L’article Interpol recourt à l’IA pour identifier des terroristes est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Nine killed in fresh Plateau attacks
items.description: Passengers, pastor among victims By Golok Nanmwa JOS — At least nine persons have been killed in separate attacks in Barkin Ladi, Riyom and neighbouring communities in Plateau State between Saturday night and Sunday morning, heightening tension in the affected areas. Five of the victims were passengers travelling to Gana-Ropp in Barkin Ladi Local Government Area when they were attacked on Saturday night, while two others, including a pastor, were reportedly killed on their way to church at Dorowa Babuje on Sunday morning. National President of the Mwaghavul Development Association, MDA, Bulus Dabit, confirmed the killing of the five persons at Gana-Ropp, condemning the attack and calling on security agencies to track down and prosecute those responsible. Dabit lamented the loss of lives, saying the recurring attacks were causing fear and anguish among residents. He urged authorities to strengthen security in vulnerable communities and ensure residents could carry out their lawful activities without fear. Also confirming the incident, Pyem Youth Leader in Gana-Ropp, Ukasha Garaba, said five bodies had been evacuated from the area. “We evacuated the corpses of five persons from Gana-Ropp. They were passengers who were travelling as labourers,” Garaba said. He described the attack as painful, saying the victims were travelling to their destination when they were attacked. Garaba called for urgent measures to protect travellers and prevent further attacks in the area. In a separate incident, two persons, including a pastor, were reportedly killed while on their way to church at Dorowa Babuje, with tension mounting in Kantoma and surrounding communities in Barkin Ladi. A woman was also reportedly killed at Baten Wereng in Riyom Local Government Area on Saturday night, September 19, while another person was killed at Ratyidi in Fan District. Spokesman of the Berom Youth Moulders, BYM, Rwang Tengwong, confirmed the attacks and condemned the killings. Tengwong described the incidents as worrisome and called on security agencies to urgently strengthen their presence in the affected communities. “We condemn these attacks in the strongest terms and call on the security agencies to urgently strengthen their presence in the affected communities. The killing of innocent people must stop,” he said. He said the fresh attacks had further heightened fear among residents and urged authorities to investigate the incidents and arrest and prosecute those responsible. Tengwong also appealed to residents to remain calm and vigilant while urging security agencies to take proactive measures to protect lives and property. Meanwhile, several cattle were reportedly killed or stolen at Dorowa Maranba and the Kantoma axis at about 3am on Sunday. Secretary of the Miyetti Allah Cattle Breeders Association of Nigeria, MACBAN, in Barkin Ladi, Gambo Abubakar, confirmed reports of cattle being stolen in the area. He urged security agencies to investigate the incident and take steps to restore calm in the affected communities. The post Nine killed in fresh Plateau attacks appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Tourisme/Lélouma : À la découverte de Touguihoî, le trésor caché des montagnes de Korbé
items.description: Niché au cœur du Fouta-Djallon, le site naturel de Touguihoî fascine par ses rochers sculptés par la nature et ses paysages verdoyants. Malgré un accès difficile qui relève du parcours du combattant, ce joyau de la sous-préfecture de Korbé (préfecture de Lélouma) offre un spectacle époustouflant qui mérite le détour. Guinéenews vous propose une immersion dans une merveille méconnue du tourisme guinéen. Après les légendaires échelles de Djinkan, l’ouest de la région administrative de Labé abrite une autre merveille de la nature ; les rochers de Touguihoî. Situés dans la sous-préfecture de Korbé, à l’est du chef-lieu Lélouma, ces blocs de pierre monumentaux dressent un décor à la fois sauvage et poétique. Sur place, l’échelonnement naturel des roches et la beauté spectaculaire du paysage continuent de fasciner les dizaines de visiteurs qui tentent l'aventure chaque semaine. C’est au village de Bourouwal, à l’entrée de la sous-préfecture de Korbé, que se dresse cet endroit féerique, devenu une escale incontournable pour les passionnés de nature et d’évasion. En cette saison des pluies, le spectacle est d'autant plus grandiose. La verdure luxuriante contraste avec les rochers soigneusement nettoyés par les averses. « Il faut le vivre pour le comprendre : cet endroit est exceptionnel. C’est comme si quelqu’un était venu superposer ces rochers les uns sur les autres avec une précision millimétrée », s’enthousiasme Mamadou Alpha Bah, un visiteur rencontré sur les lieux. Pour contempler cette œuvre de la nature, il faut toutefois armer son courage d'une bonne dose de patience. Le trajet s'apparente à un véritable parcours du combattant. Si votre véhicule (auto ou moto) réussit à vous mener jusqu’à Bourouwal, la suite du voyage s'effectue impérativement à pied. Et pour atteindre le sommet, les randonneurs doivent traverser au moins trois marigots ; escalader des parois rocheuses ; arpenter des vallées escarpées en s'accrochant parfois aux branches et aux lianes. Arrivé au rocher principal, l'effort laisse immédiatement place à l'émerveillement. Le point de vue offre une vue panoramique exceptionnelle sur Korbé, la préfecture de Lélouma et l'immensité du Fouta-Djallon, avec ses savanes, ses plaines et ses forêts à perte de vue. « Malgré la pénibilité du trajet, dès qu'on arrive au sommet, on oublie toute fatigue. L'air y est d'une pureté rare dans un environnement 100 % naturel », témoigne Maladho Barry. Touguihoî ne se résume pas à ses seuls rochers. À quelques kilomètres du village, le site abrite également de magnifiques chutes d'eau et une piscine naturelle. Ce coin d'eau est devenu le lieu de rendez-vous quotidien de la jeunesse locale, qui s'y retrouve pour se baigner ou laver du linge dans une ambiance conviviale. Véritable chef-d'œuvre de Dame Nature, Touguihoî possède tous les atouts pour devenir un pôle touristique majeur en Guinée. Cependant, sans aménagements routiers ni infrastructures d'accueil, ce potentiel reste largement sous-exploité. Comme le plaide Maladho Barry : « L’État doit tout faire pour aménager ce site afin que la Guinée puisse enfin profiter pleinement de cette richesse naturelle » lance-t-il avant de soutenir qu’il est grand temps de désenclaver ces trésors du Fouta pour faire briller le tourisme guinéen à l'échelle internationale.

items.title: La Tunisie reprend sa place dans les Guides Verts Michelin
items.description: La Tunisie fait son retour, après dix ans d’absence, dans la collection des Guides Verts Michelin consacrés au voyage et à la découverte de destinations. Le nouveau «Guide Vert Tunisie», qui sera disponible en librairie et en ligne à partir du 25 septembre 2026, a été présenté le 15 septembre à Paris, au pavillon tunisien de la 48 e édition de l’IFTM Top Resa — le principal salon professionnel français du tourisme, qui s’est tenu du 15 au 17 septembre. Ce volume de 432 pages propose des itinéraires, des cartes, des adresses, des activités ainsi qu’une sélection de sites classés selon le système traditionnel des étoiles Michelin. Parmi les lieux spécifiquement mis en avant par l’éditeur figurent Carthage, Sidi Bou Saïd et Djerba. Le guide mise également sur la diversification de l’offre touristique tunisienne au-delà du traditionnel segment balnéaire, en valorisant le patrimoine culturel, les régions de l’intérieur et le Sahara. Parmi les expériences proposées par Michelin figurent les sources thermales de l’oasis de Ksar Ghilane, des séjours dans le désert et la visite des habitations troglodytiques de Matmata. Le retour de la Tunisie coïncide avec le centenaire des guides de voyage Michelin, lancés en 1926. La collection, désormais intitulée «Guides Michelin Voyage & Cultures» , est consacrée non seulement à la visite des lieux, mais aussi à la découverte du patrimoine et des cultures des destinations. L’article La Tunisie reprend sa place dans les Guides Verts Michelin est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: I didn’t abandon Gov Yusuf; I still like him — Kwankwaso
items.description: The Leader of the Kwankwasiyya Movement, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, says he is willing to reconcile with Gov. Abba Yusuf of Kano State. It will be recalled that Yusuf, a staunch adherent of the Kwankwasiyya Movement, won the election in 2023 under the New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP), and later defected to the All Progressives Congress (APC). The development resulted to serious frosty relationship between Kwankwaso and Yusuf, whom he served as his aide in the last 40 years. However, in an interview with BBC Hausa Service, posted on his verified social media handle, Kwankwaso said he can forgive and reconcile with Yusuf, if he so wishes. Kwankwaso said he didn’t abandon nor ask Yusuf to change his political party. He added that “I didn’t abandon him, didn’t ask him to go or dismiss him, I still like him.” Kwankwaso, who is also the running mate to Peter Obi, the Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), said he was not a vengeful person and always forgives those who wronged him. He said that he forgave former Gov. Abdullahi Ganduje, in spite of several wrongdoings meted out against him. “How many times did I have issues with Ganduje? He challenged me on several occasions. “In 2007, when we were in the Ministry of Defence, he was my Special Assistant (SA), but they held meetings to bring me down because I contested with them. “In spite of the misgivings, I put Ganduje forward and supported him, but he failed,” he said. Kwankwaso, who said he never considered himself a leader who dictates or directs people on what to do, added that he is still in politics, and not an armchair politician. He explained that “I’m not God. So, if Yusuf or whoever wishes to come, you need to have patience, have a large heart and compassion because not all will play along your line. “You don’t expect everybody to act, behave or think like you do, because everyone has his way of reasoning, age, background and educational qualifications. “So, if I am not forgiving, we will not put Ganduje forward; the situation is the same with Yusuf. “We don’t ask for a dime from each of them to get our endorsement and tickets; we don’t sale our candidature.” The post I didn’t abandon Gov Yusuf; I still like him — Kwankwaso appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Élections territoriales : Me Abdoulaye Tine clarifie ses propos après son passage à la RTS
items.description: Après son passage dans l’émission « Nay Leer » de la RTS, vendredi 18 septembre 2026, Me Abdoulaye Tine, ministre-conseiller et porte-parole de la Présidence de la République, a tenu à apporter une mise au point sur ses propos relatifs aux prochaines élections territoriales. Dans une déclaration, il précise n’avoir « annoncé ni date d’élection, ni message du Chef de l’État à la Nation ». Selon lui, son intervention portait essentiellement sur le cadre juridique applicable à l’organisation des élections territoriales ainsi que sur les prérogatives conférées au président de la République par les textes. Cette précision intervient après plusieurs articles de presse ayant rapporté ses propos comme annonçant une prochaine adresse du chef de l’État aux Sénégalais sur le calendrier électoral. Au cours de l’émission, Me Tine avait notamment déclaré : « Maintenant écoutons le Président pour voir ce qu’il dira aux Sénégalais et l’argument qu’il leur donnera. Je pense que quand il s’exprimera, tout le monde comprendra. Il s’exprimera dans pas longtemps ». Dans sa mise au point, le porte-parole de la Présidence insiste toutefois sur le fait que le chef de l’État demeure maître du moment et des modalités de ses prises de parole. « Le Président de la République choisit seul le moment et la forme de ses prises de parole », souligne-t-il. Me Abdoulaye Tine rappelle également le rôle des canaux institutionnels de la Présidence dans l’annonce de toute éventuelle intervention présidentielle. « Lorsqu'il décide de s'adresser aux Sénégalais, la Présidence en informe le public par ses canaux officiels », précise-t-il.

items.title: Michelle Bachelet retire sa candidature pour le poste de Secrétaire Générale des Nations Unies
items.description: L'ancienne présidente chilienne Michelle Bachelet a annoncé, samedi, le retrait de sa candidature au poste de secrétaire générale des Nations Unies, mettant fin à une campagne lancée en février avec le soutien initial du Chili, du Brésil et du Mexique. Dans un message publié sur ses réseaux sociaux, Mme Bachelet a assuré ne pas regretter d'avoir relevé ce « grand défi », estimant que sa candidature avait contribué à porter l'idée que la prochaine personne appelée à diriger l'ONU soit une femme d'Amérique latine, indépendante et attachée aux principes de la Charte des Nations Unies. L'ancienne cheffe de l'Etat a également évoqué un contexte international “défavorable”, affirmant qu'elle poursuivrait son engagement international en faveur de la paix, de la sécurité, du développement durable et des droits humains. Son retrait intervient au lendemain d'une troisième consultation informelle au Conseil de sécurité qui lui a été défavorable, selon des médias chiliens citant des sources diplomatiques. Dans un communiqué, le gouvernement chilien a indiqué « prendre acte » de la décision de Mme Bachelet, rappelant avoir retiré en mars son soutien à sa candidature après avoir notamment évalué « la dispersion des candidats dans la région et son impact sur les possibilités de succès ». L'Exécutif a précisé que cette décision avait été prise au regard des priorités de la politique étrangère du pays et rappelé que Santiago n'avait, depuis lors, soutenu aucun autre candidat. Il a parallèlement réaffirmé son attachement au multilatéralisme, tout en plaidant pour une « profonde réforme » du système des Nations Unies. La candidature de Michelle Bachelet avait été officiellement présentée en février par le Chili, le Brésil et le Mexique. Son pays avait retiré son parrainage le 24 mars, invoquant le contexte de l'élection, la dispersion des candidatures latino-américaines et des divergences avec certains acteurs déterminants du processus. Ancienne Haute-Commissaire des Nations Unies aux droits de l'Homme (2018-2022) et première directrice exécutive d'ONU Femmes (2010-2013), Mme Bachelet avait néanmoins choisi de poursuivre sa campagne avec le soutien du Brésil et du Mexique. The post Michelle Bachelet retire sa candidature pour le poste de Secrétaire Générale des Nations Unies appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: SAMAO 2026 : IAMGOLD Essakane SA rafle le prix du meilleur exposant et cinq autres distinctions
items.description: La 8e édition de la Semaine des activités minières d’Afrique de l’Ouest (SAMAO), couplée à la première édition de la Semaine de l’énergie, des mines et des hydrocarbures de l’Alliance des États du Sahel (SEMH-AES), a consacré IAMGOLD Essakane SA comme meilleur exposant. La distinction a été remise lors de la soirée de clôture, tenue le vendredi 18 septembre 2026 à la salle des banquets de Ouaga 2000. Au terme de cinq jours d’expositions, de rencontres d’affaires, de sessions B to B et de panels, l’entreprise minière s’est illustrée dans plusieurs catégories. La clôture de la SAMAO 2026 a en effet été marquée par une pluie de distinctions en faveur des acteurs ayant contribué à l’animation et à la réussite de l’événement. Parmi eux, IAMGOLD Essakane SA s’est particulièrement démarquée en décrochant le premier prix dans la catégorie du meilleur exposant. Les distinctions… L’entreprise devance ainsi COOP-CA Burkina Mine, classée deuxième, et West African Resources, qui occupe la troisième place. Cette récompense vient couronner la participation d’IAMGOLD Essakane SA à ce rendez-vous consacré aux secteurs minier, énergétique et des hydrocarbures. Le prix du meilleur exposant n’est toutefois pas la seule distinction attribuée à l’entreprise. IAMGOLD Essakane SA a également reçu le prix du sponsor Or, celui du meilleur stand, ainsi que le prix de l’excellence pour ses efforts en matière d’environnement et de gestion énergétique. L’entreprise s’est aussi vu décerner le prix du meilleur leadership féminin. Ces différentes distinctions placent IAMGOLD Essakane SA au cœur de la cérémonie de reconnaissance organisée à l’issue de la 8e édition de la SAMAO. La Mine IAM Essakane SA a raflé le meilleur prix à la SAMAO 2026 Selon les organisateurs, elles viennent saluer la participation et la contribution des entreprises, des exposants, des chercheurs et des partenaires à la réussite de l’événement. Il faut retenir que la SAMAO 2026 s’est tenue autour du thème : « Gouvernance des ressources extractives : enjeux géopolitiques, défis et opportunités pour les États africains ». Elle a été organisée conjointement avec la première édition de la SEMH-AES, offrant ainsi un cadre d’échanges sur les enjeux liés aux ressources extractives, à l’énergie et aux hydrocarbures dans l’espace de l’Alliance des États du Sahel. Lire aussi : Tidiane Barry (DG de Essakane SA) : « La gouvernance est le fil conducteur de la gestion responsable des ressources extractives » Minute.bf

items.title: Tidiane Barry (DG de Essakane SA) : « La gouvernance est le fil conducteur de la gestion responsable des ressources extractives »
items.description: En marge de la 8e édition de la SAMAO et de la 1re Semaine de l’énergie, des mines et des hydrocarbures de l’AES, le Directeur général d’Essakane SA est, par le détour d'un entretien, revenu sur l’engagement de la mine aux côtés des États du Sahel et sur les chantiers structurants du secteur. Les travaux se sont tenus à Ouagadougou du 14 au 19 septembre 2026. Sponsor or de la 8e édition de la Semaine des activités minières d’Afrique de l’Ouest (SAMAO), couplée cette année à la 1re édition de la Semaine de l’énergie, des mines et des hydrocarbures de la Confédération des États du Sahel (SEMH-AES), IAMGOLD Essakane SA confirme son statut de partenaire historique de la grand-messe minière ouest-africaine. Pour cette huitième édition, placée sous le thème « Gouvernance des ressources extractives : enjeux géopolitiques, défis et opportunités pour les États africains », le choix de la thématique résonne comme une évidence pour Tidiane Barry, patron de la plus grande mine d’or du Burkina Faso. « Quand on parle de ressources extractives, la gouvernance est toujours au début et à la fin. C’est une affaire de gouvernance », insiste-t-il. Pour Tidiane Barry la participation à cette édition couplée SAMAO-SEMH-AES revêt une dimension stratégique supplémentaire Selon Tidiane Barry, c’est la qualité de la gouvernance qui détermine la capacité d’un État à transformer une ressource naturelle en levier de développement durable. « C’est la bonne gouvernance qui permet que ces ressources soient exploitées de façon responsable, qu’il y ait de la création de richesses de façon optimale, et aussi qu’il y ait une juste répartition de ces richesses-là entre les différentes parties prenantes », a-t-il développé. Le Directeur général de Essakane SA a plaidé en faveur de cadres législatifs et réglementaires solides, garants d’une stabilité et d’une sécurité juridique pour les investisseurs, tout en assurant une redistribution équitable de la rente minière. Pour IAMGOLD Essakane SA, la participation à cette édition couplée SAMAO-SEMH-AES revêt une dimension stratégique supplémentaire. L’intégration des pays de l’Alliance des États du Sahel (AES) dans la réflexion sur la gestion des ressources extractives constitue, aux yeux de Tidiane Barry, une avancée majeure. « Nos États sont en train de créer des cadres qui permettent d’amener une conjonction d’efforts, de facteurs, pour harmoniser un peu la gestion responsable des ressources naturelles et puis avoir une vision commune pour ces pays-là. Je pense que ça tombe à point nommé. C’est très bien pour notre espace », a-t-il félicité. Le DG de Essakane SA a situé l’engagement de la Mine dans une trajectoire de longue haleine. « Essakane SA a toujours été un leader au niveau des bonnes pratiques dans l’industrie minière », a-t-il affirmé. Il a cité en exemple le contenu local, un chantier sur lequel la mine a joué un rôle précurseur bien avant que le législateur burkinabè ne s’en empare. « Aujourd’hui, ça a été légiféré. Mais Essakane a poussé l’ensemble des acteurs dans cette thématique du contenu local depuis bien longtemps », a souligné Tidiane Barry. Le Burkina Faso a effectivement adopté en juillet 2024 une loi dédiée au contenu local dans le secteur minier, qui définit des mécanismes de développement des capacités nationales, de transfert de technologie et de sous-traitance aux entreprises locales. L'équipe dynamique de IAM Essakane SA Même logique s’agissant du capital humain. Le Directeur général met en avant la politique de l’entreprise en faveur de l’emploi national et de la relève. Les chiffres officiels confirment cette orientation : Essakane affiche un taux de 98 % de nationaux parmi ses effectifs, avec 2 402 employés en 2024. La mine a également scellé en octobre 2025 une convention avec la Direction générale des examens, de la certification et des concours pour la validation des acquis de l’expérience de ses employés. Sur le volet environnemental, Tidiane Barry a revendiqué une position de précurseur. « La réhabilitation progressive et autres, on voit bien qu’Essakane est toujours précurseur en la matière », a-t-il assuré. Cette dimension est d’autant plus sensible que le Gouvernement burkinabè a annoncé une application stricte de la réglementation relative au Fonds de réhabilitation et de fermeture de la mine à compter de 2026, avec obligation pour les sociétés minières de soumettre leurs plans de fermeture conformément au Code minier de 2024. Lire aussi : SAMAO 2026 : Une conférence publique pour penser l’avenir des ressources extractives de l’AES Mathias KAM Minute.bf

items.title: Drones hit Moscow as Russians go to polls
items.description: Russians headed to the polls on Sunday for a third and final day of tightly controlled parliamentary elections set to strengthen the Kremlin’s grip on power, as Ukraine launched a barrage at the capital Moscow. The ruling United Russia party, which backs President Vladimir Putin and has won every parliamentary election in Russia since 2003, is widely expected to secure another victory against the backdrop of the Ukraine war, now grinding through its fifth year. Russia’s Supreme Court struck the anti-war Yabloko party off the ballot weeks before the vote, while all other parties cleared to run back Putin and the Ukraine offensive. While the results are unlikely to offer many surprises, the election is the first since Moscow launched its Ukraine military campaign in 2022 and could offer clues about public opinion towards the conflict, Europe’s deadliest since World War II. Putin has urged Russians to take part, casting the vote as a show of support for Moscow’s troops and an “answer to those who want to weaken Russia”. The final day of voting was marred by the deaths of two people — a 44-year-old woman and an elderly man, according to Moscow regional Governor Andrey Vorobyov — in Ukrainian drone attacks in the capital that wounded some 20 others. Moscow’s Mayor Sergei Sobyanin accused Kyiv of attempting to interfere with the poll, saying Russian air defences had shot down more than 1,600 Ukrainian drones, 450 of which were heading towards the Russian capital. “The unprecedented attack was clearly planned with the aim of disrupting the elections. The enemy did not succeed,” Sobyanin said on Telegram. Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky praised the strikes, saying: “Our long-range responses had a very significant impact in the Moscow region last night.” A Ukrainian drone strike also hit a bus in part of the country’s southern Kherson region occupied by Moscow, killing two people, including a member of the electoral commission, according to the authorities. – Mobilisation rumours – Campaigning has been limited in the polls, which will determine all 450 seats for Russia’s lower house State Duma and which were set to close at 1800 GMT. United Russia’s main challengers — the Communist Party, the ultra-nationalist LDPR, A Just Russia and New People — all support the war and Putin. Yabloko, a liberal party that has called for an end to the fighting, was barred from running its federal list by Russia’s Supreme Court, although its candidates remain on the ballot in some single-mandate constituencies. Police arrested one of the party’s election observers on Saturday, Yabloko said, while one of its former regional chairs was jailed last month for 11 years. Some fear the post-election period in Russia will bring about a new military mobilisation, similar to the 2022 call-up of 300,000 reservists that triggered an exodus of draft-age men from Russia. Putin has denied such plans. The election also comes as Ukrainian drone strikes cause increased disruption and fuel shortages inside Russia, hitting as far as Siberia and the Urals. In Moscow, one voter told AFP on Saturday they were frustrated by the state of the economy. “Many people have lost their jobs. Wages are now falling rather than rising,” Diana, 30, said. Another voter, 71-year-old Tatiana, said she had voted for United Russia. “It is the largest party, the hardest-working and most productive,” she said. – Cyberattacks – Putin’s political opponents have mostly been driven into exile, while his main rival Alexei Navalny died in an Arctic prison in 2024. Russia’s exiled opposition has urged anti-Kremlin Russians not to boycott the elections but instead vote “against Putin’s party”. Navalny’s widow Yulia Navalnaya called on anti-war Russians to collectively cast their ballots at noon on Sunday, a tactic that drew crowds in the 2024 presidential election. Yabloko disagreed, arguing that it was better not to vote. “You are suggesting that we once again go, like sheep, dancing to their tune, and vote for those who have caused the deaths of people in Russia and Ukraine?” party chairman Nikolay Rybakov said earlier this week. Russia’s top electoral official said Saturday Moscow’s electronic voting system had been hit by “powerful” cyberattacks. She also warned that saboteurs had severed communication lines in Russia’s far east, in an apparent attempt to frustrate the voting. “We view the incident as a deliberate act of sabotage and an attempt to disrupt voting in the region,” Ella Pamfilova, chair of Russia’s Central Election Commission, was quoted as saying by state news agency TASS. The post Drones hit Moscow as Russians go to polls appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: North Korea fires ballistic missile into East Sea: Seoul
items.description: North Korea fired a ballistic missile off its east coast on Sunday, South Korea’s military said, days after Pyongyang reaffirmed its status as a nuclear-armed state. The launch came eight days after North Korea fired multiple short-range ballistic missiles towards the East Sea — also called the Sea of Japan — as part of what it later described as a joint firepower drill. It also followed Pyongyang’s rejection this week of a resolution by the UN nuclear watchdog demanding that it halt its nuclear activities. “Our military detected a ballistic missile launched from the Wonsan area of North Korea towards the East Sea at around 3pm (0600 GMT),” South Korea’s joint chiefs of staff said in a statement. The military said it had stepped up surveillance and vigilance for possible additional launches, while South Korea, the United States and Japan were “closely sharing information” on the missile. The office of the Japanese prime minister also confirmed the launch, saying on X that the projectile was a “suspected ballistic missile”. Japan’s defence ministry later said the projectile had “already fallen”, without giving further details. South Korea’s presidential National Security Office convened an emergency security meeting following the launch to review Seoul’s response and assess the launch’s impact on national security, the presidential office said. The government called on Pyongyang to “immediately cease” its ballistic missile launches, describing Sunday’s firing as a “grave act” that violated UN Security Council resolutions. North Korea accused “hostile forces” of seeking to end the country’s nuclear programme during this week’s General Conference of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA). A foreign ministry spokesperson said the IAEA resolution “has no effect on the DPRK’s position as a nuclear weapons state”, using the acronym for North Korea’s official name. North Korea has legally enshrined its status as a nuclear-armed state, with its leadership declaring the country’s atomic arsenal permanent and irreversible. Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of the North Korean leader, recently said the country’s nuclear-armed status was “absolute”, and called those hoping for its denuclearisation “idiots”. US President Donald Trump said in August that North Korea possessed 57 “very powerful” nuclear weapons, while South Korea has put the figure at between 80 and 120.

items.title: Littérature : Saïdou Maïga publie « Le Maire de Falangountou », un témoignage sur la gestion communale
items.description: L’actuel ambassadeur du Burkina Faso à Dakar, au Sénégal, Saïdou Maïga, vient d’ajouter une corde à son arc avec la publication de son premier ouvrage, intitulé « Le Maire de Falangountou ». Fort de 187 pages, ce livre revient sur son expérience à la tête de cette commune. L’ouvrage a été dédicacé le mardi 15 septembre 2026 à Ouagadougou, en présence de nombreux parents, amis et connaissances venus pour la circonstance. Dans ce livre, l’auteur passe en revue son passage à la tête de la commune rurale de Falangountou, entre 2016 et 2020. Il y évoque notamment son élection, la gestion des affaires communales, le règlement du conflit sous-jacent à la chefferie coutumière, la restauration de l’autorité municipale ainsi que les sacrifices consentis pour améliorer la mobilisation et l’utilisation des ressources. Saïdou Maïga expliquant son œuvre… Saïdou Maïga met également en évidence les négociations menées avec les sociétés minières en vue de soutenir des secteurs prioritaires tels que l’accès à l’eau, l’éducation, la santé et l’autonomisation économique des jeunes et des femmes. « Le 20 juin 2016, lorsque je me suis assis dans le fauteuil du maire qu’avait occupé mon père, les larmes me sont venues. Je mesurais ce qui me reliait à lui, mais aussi la tâche qui m’attendait. Il fallait désormais répondre aux habitants par mon propre travail », a confié l’auteur. Ancien enfant de troupe et inspecteur des impôts, puis engagé dans différentes responsabilités publiques, Saïdou Maïga affirme que c’est à Falangountou qu’il s’est forgé, grâce aux conseils de son défunt père. « J’y ai appris combien le travail collectif compte, combien il faut expliquer ses décisions, et combien une responsabilité oblige jusqu’à la manière de la transmettre. J’ai écrit pour laisser une trace de cette expérience. Je n’ai pas tout accompli. Des projets ont été interrompus et des difficultés ont subsisté. Mais je souhaite que ce qui a été vécu puisse servir à d’autres », a-t-il indiqué. Une dédicace au baobab, l'ancien Maire de Ouagadougou Simon Compaoré Intervenant lors de la cérémonie de dédicace, le président de la délégation spéciale de Ouagadougou, Maurice Konaté, par ailleurs préfacier du livre, a souligné sa proximité professionnelle avec l’auteur. Selon lui, celle-ci lui a permis de mesurer les exigences liées à la gestion d’une collectivité territoriale. « Je sais ce qui peut représenter pour un élu local le passage d’une ambition à sa réalisation », a-t-il déclaré. Maurice Konaté a évoqué les démarches administratives, les échanges avec les services techniques, les contraintes de procédure et les attentes des populations, autant de responsabilités publiques qui exigent beaucoup d’un élu local. Le préfacier a particulièrement mis en avant les investissements réalisés grâce aux ressources minières de Falangountou, commune qui abrite le site minier d’Essakane. Il a rappelé avoir effectué plusieurs missions de contrôle des investissements financés par le fonds minier. Ces missions lui auraient permis d’apprécier directement la planification et la réalisation des infrastructures. Une photo des officiers En préfaçant ce témoignage, Maurice Konaté a estimé contribuer ainsi à la transmission d’une expérience susceptible d’intéresser les responsables territoriaux, les agents publics et les jeunes qui se préparent à servir dans l’administration. Pour information, le livre est disponible à la librairie Mercury au prix unitaire de 7 000 F CFA. Minute.bf

items.title: Jehovah’s Witnesses’ blood transfusion policy still ‘confusing’ and deadly – Humanist group says
items.description: By OLAYINKA LATONA LAGOS, Nigeria — The Humanist Enabling Life Project (HELP) has accused Jehovah’s Witnesses of maintaining a contradictory and dangerous blood transfusion policy, saying the organization’s decision to allow members to accept some blood components on “personal conscience” while keeping its ban on whole-blood transfusions is confusing and continues to cost lives. In a statement signed by Leo Igwe, director of HELP, the group said it welcomed the September 18, 2026 announcement by the Governing Body of Jehovah’s Witnesses but warned that the move did not go far enough. According to Jehovah Witness Governing Body, the decision to accept red cells, white cells, plasma or platelets from another person’s blood is a matter of personal conscience, and that each member would decide whether to donate blood for the purpose of providing components or fractions for use by another person. But it added: “The long-standing refusal of whole-blood transfusions on religious grounds, a core teaching based on the command to ‘abstain from blood’ (Acts 15:20), is unchanged.” HELP said that position remains a serious threat to public health worldwide. “Jehovah’s Witnesses should stop approbating and reprobating on blood transfusion. Its ban on blood transfusion is a harmful health policy that has had an adverse health effect on people,” Igwe said. “Stating that the organization still maintains its ban on blood transfusion while allowing it on personal grounds is confusing. It is an indication that the Jehovah’s Witnesses have not realized their grievous mistake.” Igwe who is also Vice President, Humanist International lamented that the policy has led to the death and health impairment of many people around the globe, and that the organization should acknowledge it has erred and misled members over the years. “Jehovah’s Witnesses’ controversial and despicable policy on blood transfusion has cost so many lives,” he said. “Jehovah’s Witnesses should rescind the ban without reservation and apologize to the world.” HELP also cited a case last year in Calabar, Nigeria, where it said the Basic Rights Counsel obtained a court order to treat a baby who needed a blood transfusion. According to the group, Jehovah’s Witnesses officers at the clinic connived and pressured the parent to get the baby discharged against medical advice. “No one knows what eventually happened to the baby; whether the baby died or survived,” the statement said. “There have been many cases where children died because their JW parents or family members denied them blood transfusion.” HELP said it does not want a mere easing of the prohibition. It wants Jehovah’s Witnesses to rescind the ban entirely and issue an express apology for the damage caused. items.title: JI launches protest march towards Islamabad against petroleum levy
items.description: The Jamaat-i-Islami launched its protest march towards Islamabad on Sunday, with party Emir Hafiz Naeemur Rehman warning that if the government failed to abolish the petroleum levy, the JI’s protest could turn into one to oust the government. Naeem was addressing JI supporters at Karachi’s Cantonment Station before departing for Islamabad. “In line with our strategy, people from across the country have departed for Islamabad,” he said, adding that a road caravan had also departed for the federal capital in addition to the “train march”. He said the rally would pass through Hyderabad, Landhi, Nawabshah, Rohri and Sukkur, adding that “we will invite our sisters to join us once we reach [Islamabad]”. Rehman said the purpose of the march was to help relieve the burden on the least privileged. “Instead of providing relief to the people, the government has decided that it would make the nation pay for its bad governance,” he added. “We demand that the levy extortion should end. Petrol prices would then reduce quickly and reach around Rs200 per litre. That’s when the economy could move forward.” He said that the government had increased petrol prices more than any other state in the region. “The government wants to rob the common people in times of crisis,” Naeem claimed. The JI emir said voicing complaints on social media was pointless, urging supporters to step out of their houses to protest the injustice. “For the past 36-37 days, nationwide protests have been ongoing,” he said, adding that protests were currently under way in Hyderabad, Sukkur, Mirpur Khas, Larkana, Naushahro Feroze, Rawalpindi, Gujrat and various cities of KP. “JI has mobilised entire Pakistan,” he said. “No hindrances can stop the protesters.” “When we reach Islamabad, it’s not guaranteed that the situation would remain under control,” Rehman warned. If the government tried to suppress the movement, the situation would get out of control, he said. The party posted on X that the “train march”, led by Rehman from Karachi, would reach Rohri, Sukkur to hold a rally at 8pm. The protesters would depart for Multan on Monday. The JI has been holding nationwide protests against fuel levy, which is more than Rs100 per litre. On Saturday, a government delegation, including PML-N leaders Rana Sanaullah, Ahsan Iqbal, and Salman Rafique, called on the JI leadership at its Mansoorah headquarters in Lahore, but the meeting failed to break the deadlock. During the talks, the government delegation asked the JI to postpone the long march in view of security threats. However, JI leader Liaquat Baloch said the long march would remain necessary until the levy imposed on the public was withdrawn. Talks between the JI and the government began on Sept 7. The party has been staging regular sit-ins in Lahore, Peshawar, Karachi and dozens of other locations across the country since August 16 to protest the levy. Meanwhile, PTI is also scheduled to stage its protest in the capital on Sept 27 for the release of Imran Khan, among other demands. It also turned down the government’s request to postpone the march, the party, the Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas said a day earlier. Security arrangements in capital reviewed; Pims placed on ‘high alert’ Ahead of the potential long marches, Islamabad police chief Sohail Chaudhry and Commissioner Mohammad Usman reviewed security arrangements at major entry and exit points and other key locations, APP reported. Hundreds of containers have been placed at the city’s entry points as the administration braced for back-to-back protests. During the visit, the chief commissioner said maintaining law and order was a top priority and stressed that citizens, traders, businesses, professionals and government employees should be able to carry out their lawful activities without unnecessary disruption. Furthermore, the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) was placed on “high alert”, according to a notification circulated on Saturday, a copy of which is available with Dawn . The circular directed officers and staff to “remain vigilant, readily available and fully prepared to respond in case of emergency call”. Superintendent transport was urged to ensure ambulance availability round the clock during the ‘high alert’ period until Sep 30. The circular directed that emergency, ICU, operation theatre, trauma, nursing, diagnostic, blood bank, pharmacy and other critical services would remain “fully operational with adequate backup arrangements”. “All concerned are directed to make all necessary arrangement readily in case of mass casualty situation/surge,” the circular said. “Emergency and ambulance access routes shall remain clear at all times,” it added. Islamabad’s Federal Government Polyclinic Hospital was also placed on high alert.

items.title: Finance Minister advises African governments to strengthen regional tax cooperation
items.description: Finance Minister Cassiel Ato Forson has urged African governments and regional institutions to strengthen tax cooperation to protect domestic revenue and secure the continent’s development financing needs. He said African countries must have a stronger voice in the international tax architecture and coordinate their positions more effectively on emerging global tax issues. The Minister gave the advice in a speech read for him by Mr Kweku George Ricketts-Hagan, Board Chairman of the Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA) at the opening of the 8th High-Level Policy Dialogue and 23rd General Assembly of the West African Tax Administration Forum (WATAF) in Accra. The meeting, co-hosted by the GRA and WATAF, was on the theme: “Building Stronger Tax Administrations for Revenue Mobilisation and Sustainable Development. Dr Forson said regional institutions should strengthen the capacity of member tax administrations to implement international tax standards. He said such institutions should also equip African countries to negotiate effectively and protect their legitimate tax bases in the changing international tax environment. He identified issues including base erosion and profit shifting, taxation of the digital economy and the global minimum tax as matters that had become central to Africa’s development agenda. The Minister said tax administrations could no longer operate as isolated institutions because businesses were increasingly structuring their operations across jurisdictions while capital moved rapidly across borders. He, therefore, urged African tax administrations to strengthen mechanisms for sharing taxpayer intelligence, identifying cross-border tax risks and learning from successful compliance interventions. He said regional cooperation should provide a stronger tax backbone for African countries and enable them to respond collectively to emerging challenges in international taxation. The Minister also called for greater investment in African expertise, saying the continent should reduce excessive dependence on external technical capacity and build stronger indigenous tax administration capabilities. He said revenue mobilisation must also be accompanied by efforts to address illicit financial flows, tax evasion, trade under-invoicing, smuggling and other activities that resulted in revenue leakages. He urged governments and regional bodies to embrace data, digital transformation, cross-border cooperation and professional development to build stronger, smarter and more sustainable tax administrations capable of financing development. Mr Anthony Kwasi Sarpong, Commissioner-General of GRA said African countries needed to mobilise their own domestic resources fairly, efficiently and sustainably to address development financing challenges. He said West Africa recorded real GDP growth of 4.8 per cent in 2025, with growth projected at 4.6 per cent in 2026, but the region continued to face a significant development financing gap. He urged tax administrations to broaden the tax base, formalise informal economic activities, improve the management of natural-resource revenues and strengthen information exchange among jurisdictions.

items.title: NPP accuses NDC of master-minding demolition of Ho regional office fence
items.description: James Geh, Ho Central Constituency Communications Officer of the NPP, has accused the National Democratic Congress (NDC) of deliberately targeting structures belonging to the party in Ho. The dispute has therefore centred on the NPP Ho Central Constituency Office near the Ho Sports Stadium ahead of the celebration of the 2025 National Farmers’ Day and the subsequent demolition of the fence wall of the NPP Regional Office. Mr Geh told the Ghana News Agency (GNA) that the NPP was not opposed to infrastructure development but believed the latest action was deliberate. He said the party would undertake its own infrastructure projects if it returned to government, including a proposed dual-carriage road from Noguera Junction through the Ho Technical University area. His comments and the proposed road project have also been reported in contemporary coverage of the dispute. The NDC in the Volta Region has explained that the demolition of part of the fence wall of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) Regional Office in Ho formed part of an exercise to clear structures within a road reservation. Mr Sorkpa Kafui Agbleze, Volta Regional Communications Officer of the NDC, said the exercise was not targeted at the NPP or any political party but was connected to ongoing road construction and road-opening works under the Government’s Big Push infrastructure programme. The NDC made the position in a statement issued on Friday, September 18, 2026. Mr Agbleze said other structures within the affected corridor had also been removed, including portions of structures belonging to the AME Zion Church, private properties and an old structure opposite the Guinness premises. He said the NDC’s position was that the exercise was determined by the location of structures within the designated road corridor rather than the political or institutional identity of their owners. He said the party had been informed that the NPP Regional Office fence had been identified and marked for removal since the previous year, with communication reportedly conveyed to the NPP Regional leadership through the Ho Municipal Assembly. He added that the Ho Municipal Chief Executive had made attempts to engage the NPP Regional leadership on the matter. According to Mr Agbleze, the way the exercise was conducted also showed an effort to minimise damage, saying the metal gates and other removable iron works belonging to the NPP Regional Office were taken down before the fence was demolished. He said the NDC therefore rejected suggestions that the exercise constituted political victimisation and urged political parties to avoid politicising municipal engineering and development works. He said the principle of clearing structures within approved road reservations should apply equally to political parties, religious bodies, private individuals and other institutions. The two parties’ positions come amid the broader road-opening and construction activities in Ho, with the NDC maintaining that the affected fence fell within the area required for the road works. The dispute has therefore centered on whether the demolition should be viewed primarily as an infrastructure intervention or as an action targeted at an opposition party facility.

items.title: Ghana plans stronger regional power trade with Nigeria
items.description: Ghana is exploring deeper electricity cooperation with Nigeria as part of plans to strengthen its position as a regional electricity hub, Richard Gyan-Mensah, the Deputy Minister of Energy and Green Transition, said. The Minister said Ghana was working towards expanding its regional power trade even though the country was already exporting electricity to neighbouring countries. Mr Gyan-Mensah said this on Thursday at this year’s Ghana Industrial Summit and Exhibition in Accra. The event was on a sub-theme: “Providing Reliable and Affordable Electricity to Drive Sustainable Industrial Growth.” The Minister said discussions were underway to add Nigeria to Ghana’s planned regional electricity transmission arrangements. He explained that the proposed arrangement could involve Nigeria supplying natural gas to Ghana for electricity generation, with Ghana subsequently supplying electricity back to Nigeria. Ghana, he stressed, currently had sufficient generation capacity to meet domestic electricity requirements while also participating in regional electricity trade, although additional generation would be required to meet future domestic demand. He said Ghana’s Energy Ministry currently identified electricity exports to Togo, Benin and Burkina Faso as part of the country’s regional power activities, while ongoing grid expansion was intended to support further electricity exports. Mr Gyan-Mensah stressed that regional electricity exports would not be allowed to undermine Ghana’s domestic electricity requirements. He said the government would continue investing in generation and transmission infrastructure to ensure that future domestic demand was adequately supplied. He reiterated the government’s $10 billion investment in electricity generation and transmission to meet Ghana’s projected increase in power demand through 2040. The investment requirement forms part of Ghana’s Generation and Transmission Master Plan covering the period from 2025 to 2040. In a speech read out by Mr Edward Ekow Obeng-Kenzo, the Chief Executive Officer of the Volta River Authority, he said the company remained committed to working with the government to ensure reliable and affordable electricity supply to support industrial growth. He said the Authority, with its long-standing experience in power generation, had enabled it to develop expertise in reducing system losses, improving safety standards, optimising resources and enhancing service delivery. Mr Kofi Nsiah-Poku, President of the Association of Ghana Industries, called on the government to review electricity pricing arrangements for industries, adding that rising power costs were undermining production and competitiveness. He said the withdrawal of electricity discounts previously enjoyed by some companies had resulted in increases of nearly 40 per cent in their electricity bills.

items.title: NSCDC arrests five over alleged sale of dead cattle in Yobe
items.description: By Maryam Abdul-aziz Usman, Damaturu The Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, NSCDC, Yobe State Command, has arrested five persons, including a 42-year-old woman identified as Nancy Benedict, over the alleged purchase and processing of dead cattle for human consumption. The suspects were arrested in the New Jerusalem area of Damaturu, the Yobe State capital. NSCDC Public Relations Officer, Bala Garba, said the command received intelligence on the alleged activities and placed the woman under discreet surveillance for two weeks. “We got intelligence about her activities and followed her discreetly for two weeks. We eventually saw her purchasing two carcasses for N100,000, with the intention of processing the meat for human consumption.” According to Garba, the arrest followed the surveillance operation, during which operatives allegedly witnessed the purchase of the two carcasses. The five suspects were subsequently taken into custody as the command commenced investigation into the alleged operation. The investigation is expected to establish the source and condition of the carcasses, how the meat was intended to be processed and whether any of it had already been sold or supplied to members of the public. The alleged activity has raised food safety concerns, particularly because meat from animals that die without veterinary inspection may pose health risks if processed and sold for human consumption. The NSCDC said it would continue its investigation and take appropriate action based on its findings. items.title: GRA Commissioner-General calls for stronger tax cooperation to boost regional revenue mobilisation
items.description: Anthony Kwasi Sarpong, the Commissioner-General of the Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA), has called for stronger cooperation among African tax administrations to enhance domestic revenue mobilisation and support sustainable development. He said governments across the sub-region were facing growing public financing needs and debt vulnerabilities amid increasing demands for infrastructure, social investment, climate adaptation and digital transformation. Mr Sarpong made the call at the opening of the 8th High-Level Policy Dialogue and 23rd General Assembly of the West African Tax Administration Forum (WATAF) in Accra. The meeting, co-hosted by the GRA and WATAF, was on the theme: “Building Stronger Tax Administrations for Revenue Mobilisation and Sustainable Development.” Mr Sarponge said African countries needed to mobilise domestic resources fairly, efficiently and sustainably to address their development financing challenges. He said West Africa recorded real Gross Domestic Product growth of 4.8 per cent in 2025, with growth projected at 4.6 per cent in 2026, but the region continued to face a significant development financing gap. He urged tax administrations to broaden the tax base, formalise activities in the informal economy, improve the management of natural resource revenues and strengthen information exchange among jurisdictions. Mr Sarpong said effective tax systems were central to state capacity and the social contract between citizens and governments, adding that fair and trusted tax administration could promote development and enhance business confidence. He called for greater deployment of technology, including e-filing, e-payment, digital invoicing, data analytics and artificial intelligence, to improve compliance, detect tax evasion and broaden the tax base. The Commissioner-General also urged tax administrations to build strong institutions anchored in professionalism, meritocracy, integrity, accountability and transparency. He said stronger collaboration, technological innovation and robust institutions were critical to improving revenue mobilisation across the region.

items.title: North Korea fires ballistic missile into East Sea – Seoul
items.description: North Korea fired a ballistic missile off its east coast on Sunday, South Korea’s military said, days after Pyongyang reaffirmed its status as a nuclear-armed state. The launch came eight days after North Korea fired multiple short-range ballistic missiles towards the East Sea — also called the Sea of Japan — as part of what it later described as a joint firepower drill. It also followed Pyongyang’s rejection this week of a resolution by the UN nuclear watchdog demanding that it halt its nuclear activities. “Our military detected a ballistic missile launched from the Wonsan area of North Korea towards the East Sea at around 3:00 pm (0600 GMT),” South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff said in a statement. The military said it had stepped up surveillance and vigilance for possible additional launches, while South Korea, the United States and Japan were “closely sharing information” on the missile. The office of the Japanese prime minister also confirmed the launch, saying on X that the projectile was a “suspected ballistic missile”. Japan’s defence ministry later said the projectile had “already fallen”, without giving further details. South Korea’s presidential National Security Office convened an emergency security meeting following the launch to review Seoul’s response and assess the launch’s impact on national security, the presidential office said. The government called on Pyongyang to “immediately cease” its ballistic missile launches, describing Sunday’s firing as a “grave act” that violated UN Security Council resolutions. North Korea accused “hostile forces” of seeking to end the country’s nuclear programme during this week’s General Conference of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA). A foreign ministry spokesperson said the IAEA resolution “has no effect on the DPRK’s position as a nuclear weapons state”, using the acronym for North Korea’s official name. North Korea has legally enshrined its status as a nuclear-armed state, with its leadership declaring the country’s atomic arsenal permanent and irreversible. Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of the North Korean leader, recently said the country’s nuclear-armed status was “absolute”, and called those hoping for its denuclearisation “idiots”. US President Donald Trump said in August that North Korea possessed 57 “very powerful” nuclear weapons, while South Korea has put the figure at between 80 and 120. kjk/hol The post North Korea fires ballistic missile into East Sea – Seoul appeared first on Vanguard News .
